newsitem.title: FRANCE: SocGen keeps eye on CIC - interview.
newsitem.headline: SocGen keeps eye on CIC - interview.

text.p: Ste Generale boss Marc Vienot said he was still interested in acquiring CIC bank if it is put up for sale by the government again, but he would have to seen what the conditions were.
"As I told you, we are watching everything that goes on," he said when asked in an interview in Les Echos newpaper to be published on Thursday.
A copy of the interview was supplied to Reuters.

The government called off a tender in November for the sale of 67 percent of regional banking group CIC, whose parent is state insurance company Groupe des Assurances Nationales, saying it would relaunch the privatisation later.

"If it comes back under the same conditions as last time, with a poorly provided data-room, with difficult access and confidentiality obligations encumbent only on the suitor, I'd think twice about it," Vienot was quoted as saying.
"In the case of CIC, I had made a commitment to my board not to do damage to our ratio of return on equity, or earnings per share, or our ratings. Those conditions stay the same."
Vienot added that his bank "needs to be strong in France," as it worked on its strategy of a strong domestic retail presence and an international and finance banking presence abroad.

Among the conditions imposed by the government on the sale of CIC was an obligation for the buyer to respect the regional integrity of the bank grouping and its commericial links with parent company GAN.

Societe Generale and rival French bank BNP were both in the running before the government called off the tender. But France's privatisation commission had already ruled that BNP's was the only offer that respected the government list of conditions.
